subject: empty prison cell
title: What If Police Forgot You in a Cell? In 1979 a Man Lasted 18 Days

scenes.text: What if the police locked you up and forgot? In 1979 a man lasted 18 days without water.
April 1, 1979, Hochst, Austria. Andreas Mihavecz, 18, a passenger in a car crash, is put in a basement cell.
Three officers each assume one of the others let him go. The cell is underground. Nobody hears him shout.
No food. No water. He licks the condensation off the cell walls to stay alive.
April 18. An officer on other business smells something in the basement and opens the door. He is close to death, 24 kilograms lighter.
Weeks to recover. The officers were fined about 770 euros each. He holds a record nobody wants: longest survival without food and water.

description:
What if the police forgot you existed? On 1 April 1979, 18-year-old Andreas Mihavecz was put in a basement holding cell in Hochst, Austria, after being a passenger in a car crash, and the three officers responsible each assumed another had released him.
He survived 18 days with no food and no water by licking condensation off the walls, was found close to death having lost 24 kg, took weeks to recover, and holds the Guinness World Record for the longest survival without food and water; the officers were fined.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Two years later a court awarded him 250,000 schillings in damages. Which survival-without story should we run through next?
